script: Tides are caused mostly by the Moon's gravity pulling on Earth's oceans. Most coasts get two high tides and two low tides about every day. The Sun pulls on the oceans too, but less strongly. When the Sun and Moon line up, at new and full moon, tides are extra high. Those are called spring tides, even though they happen all year. Canada's Bay of Fundy has the world's highest tides, rising up to about 16 meters. Follow Pixel Abyss for more strange facts from the deep.
